title: Enhanced piezocatalytic properties in the spin-coated PVDF/ZnO films  via  hot-pressing
content: Enhancing the piezoelectric response and wettability of piezocatalytic films is important for improving their pollutant degradation performance in aqueous environments. In this study, poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)/ZnO (PZ) films with different ZnO contents were fabricated by spin coating, and hot-pressing was applied as a post-treatment to fabricate hot-pressed PVDF/ZnO (PZ-HP) films with further improved piezoelectric and surface properties. The structural and surface properties, piezoelectric responses, and methylene blue (MB) degradation performance of the PZ and PZ-HP films were compared. The formation of the electroactive β-phase of PVDF was promoted with increasing ZnO content. PZ20 and PZ20-HP, which contained the same amount of ZnO, were compared to evaluate the effects of hot-pressing. The β-phase fraction increased from 46.2% to 51.8%, while the piezoelectric output voltage increased from 0.099 to 0.169 V. The water contact angle decreased from 110.8° to 67.3°, indicating improved wettability of the PZ20-HP film. The high Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area and porosity of the films were maintained after hot-pressing. The BET specific surface areas were 44.84 ± 0.78 and 45.95 ± 0.97 m2 g−1, and the porosities were 83.25 ± 1.14% and 83.39 ± 0.43% for PZ20 and PZ20-HP, respectively. Along with this increase in the piezoelectric response and wettability, PZ20-HP showed an increase of approximately 2.3 times in the apparent kinetic rate constant, leading to an MB degradation efficiency of 98.8% after 180 min, compared with 87.4% for PZ20. This study indicates that enhanced piezocatalytic performance of PVDF/ZnO films can be obtained via hot-pressing, which simultaneously improves their piezoelectric response and wettability without compromising their surface area or porosity.
